note: Monday 10 Aug in-session run (CLI logged out since 4 Aug; it aborted cleanly at 07:02 with exit 78). 21 items verified, 1 dropped. This run graded our own Sunday forward call on oil and reports it as a partial miss. It also caught two data-quality traps: a wrong reference price that would have inflated the apparent oil move 2.7x, and futures-vs-cash comparison errors (S&P future vs cash record; Nasdaq 100 future vs Nasdaq Composite; Dec gold vs spot). One gap is declared rather than filled: no Hang Seng futures level could be confirmed.

items.headline: OUR CALL, GRADED: oil gapped up — but ~1%, not dollars, and it gave half back within two hours
items.summary: Sunday we said crude had over-discounted a Hormuz reopening and to watch the futures open. Verdict: directionally right, magnitude overstated. Brent Oct-26 opened and traded to $84.36 vs Friday's $83.55 settle (+1.0%); WTI Sep-26 $78.75 vs $78.18 (+0.73%). At the highs the pop was larger — Brent 84.97 (+1.7%), WTI 79.41 (+1.6%) — but roughly half faded within about two hours. Independent readings put the move between +0.73% and +1.0%; all reconcile to Friday's settles. Our "over-discounted" framing implied asymmetric upside; what printed was a spike sellers met.
items.actionable: Log this as a partial miss, not a win. For the oil sleeve it is a small positive mark, not a re-rating. The level that matters now: if Brent loses Friday's $83.55 settle during Asian hours, the weekend escalation has been fully round-tripped and the reopening trade reasserts.

items.headline: DATA TRAP CAUGHT: a bad reference price would have made that call look 2.7x better than it was
items.summary: Investing.com's Brent page quotes the price correctly ($84.36) but states a previous close of $82.21 — not Friday's $83.55 ICE settle — headlining +2.62%. TradingEconomics' change fields also fail to reconcile: its Brent delta implies a $83.29 prior close, and its gold/silver deltas (+2.44%, +3.32%) are demonstrably FRIDAY's moves being shown as current. Barchart and oilprice.com both reconcile exactly to the real settles. Had the dashboard taken the headline percentage, it would have reported our own forecast as 2.7x more correct than reality.
items.actionable: New standing rule for this pipeline: only trust a published percent-change when the quoted previous close matches the known prior settle; otherwise compute the delta manually. This is the second time a self-flattering number nearly reached your dashboard.

items.headline: Iran hardens further: six published conditions for reopening, and "no possibility of resuming negotiations"
items.summary: Tehran published six conditions for reopening the strait, and Foreign Minister Araghchi said Sunday there is "no possibility of resuming negotiations" with the US, even while describing the Oman lane deal as "very close". Trump said the US is "low-keying it", leaning on economic pressure. The gap between the two positions widened rather than narrowed over the weekend.
items.actionable: This is why crude did not gap dollars: a reopening was never actually imminent, so there was less mispricing to correct than we implied. It also means the Gulf risk premium is structural for now, not a headline spike.

items.headline: Houthis claim a drone strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery; Saudi confirms the fire was extinguished, no casualties
items.summary: Houthi forces claimed a drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery early Sunday. Saudi Arabia confirmed a fire that was extinguished with no casualties. Separately, Hormuz traffic is running about 33% below normal.
items.actionable: The conflict is widening beyond the strait to Saudi production infrastructure. Combined with traffic down a third, this is a slow supply squeeze rather than a single event — supportive for energy and, indirectly, for the metals bid.

items.headline: WEDNESDAY IS THE WEEK: US July CPI and Tencent Q2 results land on the same day
items.summary: US July CPI is released Wednesday 12 August at 08:30 ET, and Tencent reports interim results the same day with an interim dividend on the agenda. September Fed hike odds sit at roughly 40-44% after Friday's payrolls contraction.
items.actionable: Two of your largest exposures resolve on one day — the levered silver leg via CPI, and your single biggest HK holding via Tencent. With SGX shut today, you have Tuesday alone to position the Singapore sleeve beforehand.

items.headline: Metals barely reacted: gold futures literally unchanged, silver +0.70%
items.summary: Gold Dec-26 futures are pinned to their prior settle of 4,399.70 — successive Sunday-evening ticks printed 4,401.51 and 4,399.30, i.e. unchanged. Silver Sep-26 is 63.943, +0.70%, with previous close confirmed at 63.499. Note the contract-vs-spot distinction: Dec gold near 4,400 is not comparable to Friday's spot close of 4,343.43, which carries no forward premium.
items.actionable: After a 20%+ week in GDX, the weekend escalation produced no follow-through and no give-back. On 1.6x leverage a +0.70% silver move is ~+1.1% on the position — immaterial. The complex is waiting for CPI, which is the real driver here, not Hormuz.

items.headline: US equity futures essentially flat — no weekend risk-off despite the tanker strike
items.summary: S&P 500 Sep-26 futures 7,772.25 (-0.10%), Nasdaq 100 Sep-26 29,872.00 (+0.12%, fading to flat), Dow Sep-26 54,044.00 (-0.20%), all measured against Friday FUTURES settles, not cash closes. Two comparison traps flagged: the S&P cash record was 7,757.64, about 22 points below the futures settle, so 7,772 is not a new high; and the Nasdaq 100 future (29,872) is a different index from the Nasdaq Composite (26,690.62) and must not be compared to it.
items.actionable: The market is treating Hormuz as contained — consistent with the muted crude response. Wednesday's CPI, not the Gulf, is the week's risk event.

items.headline: China July inflation undershoots: CPI +0.5% y/y, PPI +3.5% y/y — energy doing the deflating
items.summary: China's July CPI rose 0.5% year-on-year and PPI 3.5%, both below expectations, released Sunday 9 August by the National Bureau of Statistics. Energy is the main deflating component.
items.actionable: A soft print lands straight into this morning's HK open. Weak inflation keeps the policy-easing case alive for China, which supports your HK tech sleeve — but it also says domestic demand is not yet firing.

items.headline: SGX confirmed fully closed today for National Day — the Singapore sleeve does not mark until Tuesday
items.summary: Singapore Exchange is fully closed Monday 10 August for the National Day holiday (observed). Your Singapore banks, REITs and developers do not trade or mark today.
items.actionable: One session — Tuesday — to act on the record DBS and OCBC results or reposition ahead of Wednesday's CPI.

items.headline: Bitcoin quiet at $64,873, -0.12% in a tight overnight range
items.summary: Bitcoin traded a narrow overnight range at roughly $64,873, down 0.12%, with no weekend catalyst.
items.actionable: Second weekend running that crypto has failed to join a metals rally — the debasement trade is not moving as one.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign the Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement
items.summary: Signed Friday 7 August, a NATO-style mutual-defence arrangement between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan — landing days before the Sunday Houthi strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery.
items.actionable: Structural, not tradeable today, but it raises the ceiling on regional escalation risk that sits behind your energy and metals exposure.

items.headline: GAP DECLARED: no live Hang Seng futures level could be confirmed this run
items.summary: No Hang Seng futures quote could be verified on a loaded page before the 09:30 SGT cash open, so no HK pre-open level is published. China July credit and money-supply data are also not yet out — the PBoC release window is 10-15 August.
items.actionable: Stated as a gap rather than filled with an inferred number. Tencent, Xiaomi and SMIC open at 09:30 SGT into the soft China CPI print.
